boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Auburn record (October 13, 1863) in the Bristoe Campaign [October-November 1863]. The next morning's fight at Auburn is the separate frozen record VA041. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. NPS says Stuart had Fitzhugh Lee's and Lomax's brigades. Stuart says he advanced with Lomax's brigade and the brigades of Funsten and Gordon, left Lomax at Auburn, and had seven guns with him when cut off. Humphreys says Stuart had a brigade of cavalry among the Second Corps and Gregg's cavalry.
claims.rationale: The accounts name different Confederate brigades and give no counts; none is adopted. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Stuart says Lomax's courier about the loss of Auburn did not reach him by 9 p.m., that captured dispatches showed the enemy did not know his position, and that his six messengers got through to Lee by 1 a.m. Humphreys says Stuart communicated his situation to Lee during the night, while Meade's information on the position of Lee's army that evening was erroneous.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from interested accounts on both sides; no message log inspected.

open_questions: Lomax's and Gregg's reports and the III and II Corps reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Humphreys is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff in 1863–64, per his publisher's list. Stuart's, A. P. Hill's and Lee's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIX, Part 1, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
